request.spec:
A search box and a button list, over this sheet and every other sheet of its tree, every person
whose name or an alias contains the typed text (case ignored), one line per person as
<sheet id> <name> <due-total>, this sheet's people first in list order, then the other sheets' by
sheet id.
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
A search box and a button list, over this sheet and every other sheet of its tree, every person
whose name or an alias contains the typed text (case ignored), one line per person as
<sheet id> <name> <due-total>, this sheet's people first in list order, then the other sheets' by
sheet id.

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
I added the tree search, and `bin/e2e` passes all 4 tests in the spec: the "tree search" test and the three longer scenarios.

There's now a search box and button on the main screen. Pressing the button lists every person on this sheet and the other sheets in its tree whose name or an alias contains the typed text, case ignored. Each line reads `<sheet id> <name> <due-total>`. This sheet's people come first in list order, then the other sheets' people, by sheet id. A blank search lists everyone. The result count is cleared while a search runs, and a failed search shows an error.

- **Server:** a new read-only endpoint, `GET /api/sheets/{id}/search?text=…`, in `TreeSearchController.java` and `TreeSearchService.java` under `src/main/java/net/officefloor/hq/app/search/`. It finds the tree with the existing `SheetRepository.tree` (all ancestors and all their descendants). The due-totals come from the existing `Rollup.take`, so they match the figures shown on each sheet, with `n/a` when a person has none. It writes nothing to the store or the audit file.
- **Front end:** a service in `core/search.ts` and a panel in `features/search/search.ts`, built the same way as the audit viewer. The panel sits on the home screen after the summary.

Three behaviours the request didn't specify, so I chose them:
- Retired people are always included, whether or not "show retired" is on. The test only searches with it on.
- The search ignores the "as of" date and always uses current figures.
- Spaces at either end of the typed text are dropped before matching.

No database changes were needed.

probe.probe_text:
I made no changes. These are the figures and rules as the code names them.

## 1. Figures and the rules behind them

### What a claim shows (`features/claims/claims.ts:92-125`)
- **`claim-due`** comes from `figure(c)`. The rule, in order:
  1. If it has a `settledDue`, that frozen figure is shown.
  2. Otherwise, if it is `bound(c)` (`stated && status !== 'PENDING'`), the `statedDue` is used.
  3. Otherwise the **live due** is used: `amount × rate ÷ 100`. The rate is the one `Rates.inForce` finds for the grade the person had on the claim's date (`gradeOn`), for that date.
  4. The result then goes through `chargedCents`: the **late charge** is added, then the **floor** is applied.
  5. With no rate, it shows `n/a` (`NO_RATE`).
- **Rate in force** (`rates.ts:inForceAmong`): the rate whose from-date is the latest on or before the date. A rate with no from-date applies from the beginning of time, and none applies after its `to`. If the grade has no rate here, it falls back to the parent sheet, then that sheet's parent, up to 3 levels (`Rates.inherited`, `Sheet.parent`).
- **Rounding**: `roundsHalfUp(date)` rounds half up for a claim dated before the `policyDate` (or before the sheet's today when there is none), and half to even otherwise. A correction rounds by the date of the claim it corrects (`roundingDate`). The maths uses BigInt cents; the server uses `BigDecimal.setScale(2, rounding)`.
- **Late charge** (`lateCents`, `Sheet` "late charge"):
  - It applies only while the claim is `overdue`, and never to a correction.
  - For each full 30 days past `lateFrom`, it adds that boundary date's `latePctOn` of (figure plus earlier charges). That makes it compound, rounded the way the claim's date rounds.
  - A statement never binds it, and settling freezes it in.
- **Floor**: `floorOn(c.date)` is applied last, and not to corrections. It starts at 1.00.
- **`claim-due-by`** (`dueBy`) is fixed when the claim is added (`ClaimService.add`):
  - The number of days comes from the person's own `terms`, else `termsFor(grade on its date)`: the grade's `terms-<grade>`, else the sheet's `terms` (starting at 14).
  - That many **business days** are counted after the claim's date (`HolidayService.businessDaysAfter`, skipping weekends and holidays).
  - It does not change when terms change or the claim is re-dated. Adding a holiday works it out again for claims that are not SETTLED or VOID.
- **`claim-overdue`** (`overdue`): the claim is OPEN or PENDING, not `deferred`, and `lateFrom < today`. `lateFrom` is the due-by plus `graceOn(grade, date)`.
- **`claim-period`**: the period whose dates contain the **due-by** (`periods.of(c.dueBy)`).
- **`claim-number`** (`SheetService.nextClaimNumber`) is given when the claim is opened:
  - Normally it is `FY<yyyy>-n`, restarting each fiscal year (by `fiscalStartMonth`), and the sequence is shared across the sheet tree.
  - While the sheet's today is on or after `periodNumberingFrom`, it is `<period>-n` instead, or `X-n` for a claim in no period.
  - A voided claim keeps its number. Reassigning takes a new number.
- **`claim-stated`**: `c.stated` (the raw flag, not `bound`).
- **`claim-deferred`** (`deferredShown`): the deferred-until date is after the sheet's today, whatever the status. Only an OPEN deferred claim is left out of totals (`deferred`).
- **Other flags and fields**:
  - **`claim-late-entry`**: set if the claim was added while its period was soft-closed.
  - **`claim-batch`**: the bulk-settle batch number.
  - **`claim-split-from`**, **`claim-corrects`**, **`claim-opened-by`**, **`claim-proofs`**, **`claim-reminded`**: stored values shown as they are.
  - **`claim-log-line`**: each status line carries the due as shown at that moment (`logStatus` → `shownDue`).

### Which claims count (`claims.ts`)
- **`counts` / `ClaimStatus.counts`**: OPEN, PENDING or SETTLED. DRAFT, VOID and DELETED count nowhere.
- **`live`** = claims that count, minus those `leftOut`, minus those `deferred`.
  - **`leftOut`**: an OPEN or PENDING claim that is not `bound`, and either dated inside one of the person's holds (`heldOn`) or whose person's `retiredFrom ≤ today` (`retiredBy`).
- **`counted`** (used for claimed) = live claims minus corrections (claims with `corrects`).
- **`periodCandidates`**: every claim except those left out or deferred, whatever its status.

### What a person's row shows (`features/people/people.ts:230-352`, `figures.ts`)
- **`person-claimed`**: the sum of `amount` over `counted`.
- **`person-due-total`** (`dueCents`):
  - `sumCents` adds up `figureCents` over the person's live claims, then caps the result at the `cap` in force on today.
  - It shows `n/a` when the grade in force today has no rate **and** no claim has a kept figure.
- **`person-excess`**: how far that sum is above the cap.
- **`person-settled-total`** / **`person-open-total`**: the live SETTLED claims, and the live OPEN and PENDING claims.
- **`person-overdue-count`** / **`person-overdue-total`**: the live claims that are `overdue`.
- **`person-aged-0-30` / `person-aged-31-60` / `person-aged-61`**: live OPEN and PENDING claims, split by how many days old the claim's date is.
- **`person-active`**: they have a live OPEN or PENDING claim dated within today−29 to today.
- **`person-backing`**: for each patron, their `recentSettledCents` (frozen settled dues dated within the last 90 days) × share ÷ 100. These are added up and rounded half to even.
- **`person-cut-total`**: the person's pool cuts added up.
  - A cut is a share of the pot of a *balanced* pool (shares total exactly 100.00).
  - Retired members, members on hold, and members whose dates don't include today get 0.00, and their share is spread over the others.
  - The figure comes from the server (`pools.ts`).
- **`person-grade`**: `gradeOn(grades, today)`.
- **`person-retired`** is "a retirement date is set at all". Separately, `retiredBy` only drops claims from totals once that date is reached.
- **`person-hold`**: the person has any hold at all.
- **`person-clashing`**: their name or an alias is used on another sheet in the tree.
- **Statement fields**:
  - **`person-statement-count`**, **`person-stated-total`**, **`person-statement-date`**: values recorded when statements are taken.
  - **`ClaimService.statement`**: records the due-total and binds each counted claim to its rate figure. Held, retired-and-left-out and deferred claims are left unbound, and a PENDING claim is bound only once it is back to OPEN.
  - **`statementAsOf`**: does the same with a past date standing in for today.
  - **`cancelStatement`** (steward only): unbinds the claims that statement bound.

### Sheet totals
- **Not trimmed** (`people.ts:114-120`):
  - **`rollup-claimed-total`**, **`rollup-settled-total`**, **`rollup-open-total`**: plain sums over everyone.
  - **`rollup-overdue-count`**: the number of overdue claims across everyone.
  - **`rollup-cut-total`**: everyone's pool cuts added up.
- **Trimmed** (`trimmed`: with 3 or more people, the single highest and lowest are dropped):
  - **`rollup-due-total`** / **`header-due-total`** (`dueTotal`): the capped due-totals, skipping people who show `n/a`.
  - **`rollup-overdue-total`** / **`header-overdue-total`** (`overdueTotal`).
- **`my-due-total` / `my-overdue-total`** (`mine`): the figures of the person whose name or alias matches the signed-in user.
- **`tag-totals`**: for each tag on a claim or its person, the live dues of matching claims (counted once per tag).
- **`month-totals`**: the live dues of claims, grouped by the month of the claim's date.
- **`summary-statuses`**: claim counts per status.
- **`consolidated-*`**: the descendant sheets' figures added up, worked out on the server by `Rollup` "descendants".

### Periods (`Period.java`, `figures.ts:livePersonPeriodCents`)
- A claim belongs to the period that contains its **due-by**.
- **`period-due-total`**:
  - **While the period is open**, it is live. It counts a claim only if `statusAt(c, period.to)` counted: the status its log records at the end of the period's last day, so a claim added later doesn't count. The claim must also not be left out by a hold or deferral now. Each claim adds its due as shown now.
  - **When closed or soft-closed**, it is frozen in `closedPersonTotals` / `closedTotal`. A person added since then shows 0.00.
- **Closed**: every change to a claim in that period is refused (`refuseClosed`). **Soft-closed**: the figures are frozen but claims can still change, and a new claim added there is marked `lateEntry`.
- **Who may close and reopen**: `close` is allowed by role per the permission matrix. `reopen` is steward-only by the standing rule.
- **Auto-close**: changing the sheet's today closes each open period whose to-date plus the sheet's `graceDays` is before the new today.
- **`period-cap`**: opening a claim is refused if the person already has that many OPEN or PENDING claims in the period (`refuseOverCap`).

### Status moves and who may do what (`ClaimStatus.canBecome`, `ClaimService`, `RoleService`, `Sheet.STANDING_PERMISSIONS`)
- **Roles**:
  - A name with no role is a **clerk**.
  - A **steward** has the role, or has it delegated for today's date.
  - A **viewer** may change nothing.
  - An **archived** sheet refuses every change.
  - **Standing rule**: open, settle, void and close are allowed to clerk and steward; reassign and reopen to steward only. The sheet's permission matrix can override each of these.
- **Status moves**: DRAFT→OPEN or VOID; OPEN→SETTLED or VOID; PENDING→VOID; SETTLED→VOID.
- **Voiding a SETTLED claim** needs a steward, within 7 days of its last SETTLED log date. If the sheet has void reasons, a void must choose one of them.
- **Opening**:
  - It is refused when the due is above the `noteThreshold` (on the claim's date) and the note is empty.
  - It is refused when the period cap would be exceeded.
  - Opening sets the number and `openedBy`.
- **Settling**:
  - It is refused for the user who opened or last edited the claim, for a deferred claim, and when the due is above the proof threshold (the grade's, else the sheet's, on the claim's date) with 0 proofs.
  - The figure is the bound one, else the live one, plus the charge and floor.
  - If a clerk settles above the `clerkLimit` (the limit in force on today), the claim goes **PENDING** instead, and its due stays live.
  - If the due is `n/a`, `settledDue` stays null and the due stays live.
- **Approve / reject** (steward only, not the opener or last editor):
  - **Approve** freezes the live figure now.
  - **Reject** needs a reason and sends the claim back to OPEN, bound again by the last statement.
- **Re-settle** (steward, SETTLED claims): freezes the claim again at today's rate, grade, floor and charge.
- **Delete / restore**: only a DRAFT can be deleted, and it is restored only on the same sheet's today.
- **Edit** (DRAFT only): opening the editor locks the claim for other users. A claim with lines takes its amount from the lines.
- **Re-date** (steward, OPEN or PENDING): the due-by, number and bound figure stay as they are. A date after the person's retirement is refused.
- **Reassign**: DRAFT, OPEN or PENDING claims only. The claim gets a new number and becomes unbound.
- **Split** (OPEN, not deferred, needs `open` permission): the amount must be above 0 and below the claim's. The kept part becomes unbound, and the split-off part is a new OPEN claim.
- **Defer** (OPEN only, to a date after today): until then the claim is in no total, not overdue and can't be settled.
- **Correction**: a negative amount must name a SETTLED claim of the same person. It gets no floor and no late charge, and is not counted in claimed.
- **Adding a claim**: the date defaults to `entryDate`, else today. A claim dated after the person's retirement is refused. A `ref` already used on the sheet is refused, ignoring case.
- **Bulk settle** is all-or-nothing and makes a batch. Bulk open, reassign and re-date refuse claims one at a time.

### What the date decides
- The **sheet's today** (never the clock) decides overdue, deferral, aging, active, the cap, the clerk limit, the grade shown, retirement leaving claims out, delegations and period auto-close.
- The **claim's date** decides the grade, rate, floor, grace, terms, proof threshold, note threshold and rounding.
- Each **late-charge boundary date** decides the late percent for that step.
- **As-of mode** (`AsOf`) replays everything at the end of a chosen date and refuses every change.

### Imports, holds, retirement
- **Person import**: all-or-nothing. A line whose name matches a person updates them, recording the grade from today; any other line adds a person. Rate import is also all-or-nothing.
- **Hold**: drops a person's unbound OPEN and PENDING claims dated inside the hold from every live total. Statements leave those claims unbound, and the person's pool cut becomes 0.
- **Retirement**: once `retiredFrom` is reached, the person's unbound OPEN and PENDING claims leave the totals, and new claims dated after it are refused.
- **Merge / transfer** (steward only): carry the person's claims, frozen figures and statements to the other person or sheet.
- **Side effects**: every change also writes `ROLLUP`, `TOTALS` and `ALERT` audit lines when figures move (`Rollup.recordChanges`).

## 2. How hard it was to follow

It was hard. The due rule (settled → bound → live, then late charge and floor) is copied in at least six places:
- `figures.ts`, twice: `figureCents` and `claimDue`, plus a third variant in `livePersonPeriodCents`
- `features/claims/claims.ts` `figure()`
- `ClaimService` (`due`, `shownDue`, `liveDue`)
- `Rollup`
- `Sheet`

Who-may-do-what is spread across `RoleService`, `Sheet.allows`, `ClaimStatus` and about twenty `refuse*` checks inside a 1,180-line `ClaimService`. The comments don't always match the code either: `Claim.dueBy` in `claims.ts` says "date plus terms", while the server counts business days and puts the person's own terms first. A new developer would have to piece it together from the comments.
